account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments: the morning mill inspection, council correspondence at thirteen, and now tea with the neighbour at the east-dock cottage. I arrived at 14:28, ahead of our fifteen o'clock tea; the neighbour is here. I must return to the office for the sixteen-thirty review. No new council letters have arrived, according to the secretary, and I returned the three existing signed records to the appointments chest after reviewing them.

The unusual matter is repeated, vague talk of a bridge or port change at the bakery. Several townsfolk repeated it, sometimes mentioning the baker and neighbour and the baker carrying a sack of bread. I have not established what changed, whether anything actually changed, or its purpose. A sack of bread alone does not establish anything suspicious. I asked the neighbour about the rumours and Freight's possible concern, but received no substantive explanation. Tea may provide an opportunity to clarify this directly.

At the mill I saw 128 hay bales in the stall chest, priced at two emeralds each. I did not locate a keeper who could confirm storage conditions or deliveries, and reported those limits to the secretary rather than treating stock as proof that all arrangements are satisfactory.

Builder and the secretary are preparing a written maintenance report. Builder says the inn door worked, an authorized lantern was installed clear of the passage for four emeralds paid, and sleeping arrangements remain unverified. He also reports no visible defect at the east landing, while explicitly saying this was not a comprehensive structural inspection. These appear to be maintenance and safety checks; I have no evidence connecting them to the bakery rumours. I asked that the report preserve those limitations. The secretary has an office writable book, for which I separately supplied one emerald; that stationery expenditure is distinct from the agreed two-emerald builder inspection fee.
